source_caption:
Pressure, it changes everything. Al Pacino improvised many of his lines in The Devil's Advocate (1997). Al Pacino originally turned down the role three times, fearing the Devil would come across as "cartoonish." To seal the deal, Keanu Reeves took a massive multimillion-dollar pay cut just to ensure the studio had the budget to hire Pacino. Keanu prioritized the art over his paycheck, knowing the movie only worked if he faced a true titan. This allowed Pacino the space to improvise and "theatricalize" John Milton. This added an extra layer of authenticity to his role. Have you seen The Devil's Advocate?

source_details.title: The Devil's Advocate
source_details.synopsis: The Devil's Advocate (marketed as Devil's Advocate) is a 1997 supernatural horror film directed by Taylor Hackford, written by Jonathan Lemkin and Tony Gilroy, and starring Keanu Reeves, Al Pacino and Charlize Theron. Based on Andrew Neiderman's 1990 novel, it is about a gifted young Florida lawyer invited to work for a major New York City law firm. As his wife becomes haunted by frightening visions, the lawyer slowly realizes the firm's owner, John Milton, is the Devil. The film is an international co-production between the United States and Germany.
